text:
maria: FYI saw a small surge of resume failures this morning when the EU canary flipped. Not full outage but a weird pattern of reconnect->failback->duplicate-billing markers.

sam: Can you paste console traces? thinking it might be the route-prune change we rolled last night. :thinking:

maria: pasted snippets in #eng-platform-logs but short: many clients got 204 on proxy then retried and hit fallback route that has different quota namespace.

kevin: Oof. That's the new prune policy (prune-after=30s) — it drops the sticky lease and triggers fallback. We intended sticky->fallback to be idempotent but quota names differ.

jen: Ops-bot flagged 3 duplicate token charges; looks correlated to resume timestamps in the same 60s window.

maria: timeline: canary flip 08:12:05, first 204s at 08:12:07, client reconnect surge 08:12:10-08:12:40, duplicate charge alerts 08:12:30 onwards.

sam: Is the console showing sampling gap on resume events? I remember we lowered resume sampling to 0.5% yesterday.

kevin: Yeah the dashboard shows a drop in resume span tags after the roll; we under-sampled, so root cause visibility is poor.

maria: Repro steps local: start a long SSE stream -> flip route prune manually -> proxy returns 204 -> client resumes -> server generates two resume-ack events. Small script attached:

```
# simulate resume loop
curl -N "https://api.redwood/dev/sse?client=sim1" &
sleep 1
# flip route prune
curl -XPOST https://console.internal/route/prune?route=eu-canary
sleep 1
# trigger client reconnect
kill -HUP $!; sleep 2
```

sam: Thanks. Two quick proposals: 1) revert prune-after to 5m until quota-names are reconciled, 2) add a fallback-idempotency header so retries don't double-charge. Prefer (2) but (1) is fastest rollback.

kevin: For UX, if we go with (2) the console should surface a new field on routes: "fallback_quota_namespace" with a tooltip. Product will want that before GA.

jen: Oncall wants an immediate mitigation. Can we clobber prune-after to 300s for canary only? I'll open a hotfix if agreed.

maria: Hotfix SGTM for canary. We should also bump resume sampling to 10% for next 6 hours so SRE/observable can verify.

sam: I'll push a toggle: sampling.resume_span=0.10 and route.prune_after.eu-canary=300. Rolling now via deploy-bot.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started rollout of config changes to eu-canary. Change-id: cfg-202403. Rolling: 2/3 hosts updated.

kevin: Can we also add a temporary console alert rule: if resume-failures > 5/min and duplicate-billing > 1 then page oncall?

jen: Yes, please. I don't want to chase this at 3am.

maria: After rollback + sampling increase we still saw a couple of dup markers but rate dropped 90%. Looks like rollout was the trigger.

sam: Next steps doc says: implement fallback-idempotency header in proxy (X-Fallback-Id) + add console UI for fallback_quota_namespace + permanent increase to resume sampling for 24h after any routing rollout.

kevin: I'll file the console PR and mockup the UX for fallback namespace (link in thread).

maria: Thanks. Recording this as incident note: minimal user impact, billing duplicates small but unacceptable. Will followup with postmortem if anything recurs. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-note-saved: incident-1718776543."
